title: Streamline smart-router callpath: remove legacy shims, upgrade deps, and add deterministic routing logs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Refactor the smart routing call path to remove three legacy shims (region_shim, legacy-policy-adapter, and route-cache-facade), upgrade the policy-parser dependency from v0.9.x to v1.2.x, and introduce deterministic, structured routing logs for easier postmortem and SLO analysis. This ticket reduces runtime hot-path branching, collapses duplicated fallback logic, and centralizes routing decision telemetry so rollout engineers can validate behavior without invasive debug builds.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Remove region_shim, legacy-policy-adapter, and route-cache-facade with no functional regression: existing end-to-end routing behavior for primary customers remains unchanged.
2) Compile policy rules at startup into a decision DAG; runtime evaluation must show >=15% fewer conditional branches on p50 request path in perf traces.
3) Upgrade policy-parser to v1.2 and provide adapter layer for deprecated rule expressions; all deprecated expressions converted or safelisted with warnings in startup logs.
4) Emit deterministic routing events (trace_id, request_key, evaluated_rules, chosen_variant, fallback_reason) to structured logs (JSON) and to tracing spans.
5) All existing unit and integration tests pass; add three new integration tests covering regional failover, capacity-based fallback, and explicit customer-affinity routing.
6) Rollout gated behind feature flag smart_router_v2 with gradual ramp to 100% over 48h and automatic rollback on increased error-rate or latency regressions per SRE runbook.
updates: 2026-02-20: Spike completed — measured current hot-path: region_shim contributes ~12% of CPU samples in routing worker under p50 traffic (profiling on staging). Proposal written: compile rules to DAG + remove shims.

2026-02-25: Design review with PM and SRE — agreed on deterministic logging schema and that routing decisions must be idempotent for replay tests. Action: produce ML-friendly fields in logs (evaluated_rules_hash, score_vector).

2026-03-02: Dependency discussion — policy-parser v1.2 introduces breaking AST shape. Decided to add thin compatibility adapter that normalizes legacy AST nodes; adapter lives in routing/lib/adapter and will be removed in two sprints after rule migration tools run.

2026-03-05: First PR (github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/3124) opened: initial compiler and test harness. Runs in CI but failing two integration tests around capacity-based fallback due to different tie-breaker ordering — investigating.

2026-03-10: Tie-breaker bug root cause: legacy fallback code applied last-match preference; new compiler applies first-match. Decision: adopt deterministic first-match in compiled DAG and add migration note. Noted customer-impact for any rules relying on implicit last-match behavior; will provide migration tool and warn in startup logs.

2026-03-12: PR 3124 updated to include migration warnings and a toggle to preserve legacy last-match semantics for customers who opt-in. Integration tests pass locally. Preparing canary plan and SRE runbook updates.

2026-03-12: Blocker: one downstream service (route-metrics) consumes legacy string-format logs. Coordinate with Observability team to deploy forward-compatible parser before canary. Ticket ENG-14258 referenced for observability changes.

Next steps: finish feature-flag wiring, land PR after Observability announces backward-compatible parser, run 24h canary on non-critical region, collect telemetry and SLOs, then ramp per rollout_plan.
links: Incident reference: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2025-09-routeshadow (shows when legacy shims caused regional divergence)
risks: Rules relying on implicit last-match semantics may change behavior causing incorrect routing for a small set of customers.
policy-parser upgrade may surface previously silent rule errors leading to failed startups in early canary if not warned and migrated.
Structured log changes could break downstream consumers if the Observability parser is not updated in time.
mitigation: Add compatibility toggle to preserve legacy last-match semantics for opt-in customers during migration window.
Emit startup warnings with a list of deprecated/invalid rules and provide automated migrator tool (WIP).
Coordinate with Observability to deploy forward-compatible JSON parser before routing canary; hold canary until confirmed.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind smart_router_v2 feature flag. 2) Deploy to canary cluster in us-west for 5% of traffic for 24h. 3) Monitor routing decision parity dashboard and latency/error SLOs. 4) Ramp to 25% for 24h, then 100% over 48h if no regressions. 5) If errors exceed threshold or decision parity drops >0.5%, rollback flag immediately.
qa_plan: Unit tests for compiler and adapter; integration tests for: regional failover, capacity fallback, customer-affinity routes. Add fuzz test that compares legacy and compiled DAG outputs for 1000 random rule sets. Manual verification: run parity job that replays last 24h of routing decisions and compares chosen_variant and fallback_reason columns.
notes: We intentionally picked deterministic first-match semantics for compiled DAG to simplify reasoning and make parity tests reproducible. Long-term, remove adapter after two sprints and require rules to conform to v1.2 AST. Observability changes are the main cross-team dependency; coordinate release calendar with Platform & Observability PMs.
